correctness.rationale: For a right equilateral triangular prism with base circumradius R and half-height h>0, Haar-uniform unoriented central-plane normal, put t=h/R. A generic section crosses 3,4 or 5 prism edges/faces. Its triangle criterion is |R r cos(φ-2πj/3)|<h|w| for all j; sixfold angular symmetry yields p3=1-(6/π)arcsin(1/(2√(1+t²))). Each of nine prism edges contributes a crossing probability equal to its endpoint-vector angle/π: horizontal edge angle G=acos((t²-1/2)/(t²+1)) (six edges) and vertical angle 2atan(t) (three edges). Thus E[N]=(6G+6atan(t))/π; because support is {3,4,5}, p5=E[N]-4+p3 and p4=1-p3-p5. Positivity follows from open normal cones, while derivative p3>0 proves exact global aspect inversion. Derivative p5=6H(t)/(π(1+t²)); H strictly decreases from 1 to 3/2-√3<0, so one global p5 maximum at t≈0.53146955. Null nongeneric normals and endpoint degeneracies explicitly excluded.
